title: fix: Stale WASM package cache updates
description:
The WASM package cache can serve an outdated package binary indefinitely, causing apps to fail in the browser with errors like

```
preload error: namespace 'scales' 1.3.0 is being loaded, but >= 1.4.0 is required
```

even though repo.r-wasm.org now serves a later version.

The cache keys the re-download decision on the locally installed package version, but the binary actually downloaded is whatever version repo.r-wasm.org currently serves, which can lag behind CRAN. So if the repo lags at download time (local scales 1.4.0, repo only has 1.3.0), it stores `ref = scales@1.4.0` while the file on disk is `scales_1.3.0.tgz`. Once the repo catches up to 1.4.0, the recomputed ref still matches the stored ref, so it's a cache hit and the stale 1.3.0 binary is never replaced. The only workaround is manually deleting the cache directories and re-rendering.

The fix is to key the cache on the version actually downloaded from the repo so it self-invalidates and re-downloads once the repo catches up, remove stale `.tgz` files on re-download, skip re-downloading binaries already on disk, and cache the `available.packages()` index to keep the repeated repo lookups cheap.

title: Improve Wasm R package binary assets downloading when exporting a Shinylive app
description:
This PR contains three changes to improve the bundling of static assets for loading R package binaries into webR.

1. Switch to using `.tgz` formatted R package binaries, support for which is introduced in webR 0.4.2 (https://github.com/r-wasm/webr/pull/477). This additionally fixes bundling R-Universe packages as static assets, as it now also serves packages in this new format.
2. When downloading package libraries served via GitHub Assets, allow for compressed libraries with filename `library.data.gz`.
3. For R packages hosted by the Bioconductor repository, grab the equivalent package from R-Universe's mirror. Due to 1, this fixes exporting Shinylive apps that use bioconductor packages.

This relies on using webR v0.4.2, and so requires a new version of the Shinylive assets. So, I will open a linked PR on [posit-dev/shinylive](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinylive/tree/main) and convert this from a Draft PR once new assets are ready.

title: Fix: Allow `shinylive-r` chunks to create files in subdirectories
description:
This PR updates `build_app_resources()` so that it can create files in subdirectories, e.g.

```
## file: R/load_data.R
data <- read.csv("data.csv")
```

This would previously fail because `writeLines()` would write to `"{appdir}/R/load_data.R"` but `{appdir}/R` doesn't exist yet.

While here I also added a check, after normalizing `file$name`, to make sure that file names are specified relative to the app directory and don't escape upwards.

title: Add `SHINYLIVE_WASM_PACKAGES` environment variable
description:
Continuing the work in https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/pull/114 and earlier PRs, adds an environment variable `SHINYLIVE_WASM_PACKAGES`, defaulting to `TRUE`.

When `SHINYLIVE_WASM_PACKAGES` is set to `FALSE` or `0`, no wasm R packages are exported at all. This allows the user to turn off the mechanism when using Shinylive with Quarto, should they want to.

Closes https://github.com/quarto-ext/shinylive/issues/60.

title: Avoid `LinkingTo` dependencies in package resolution
description:
Packages listed under `LinkingTo` are required for _building_ dependent packages, but not loading them at runtime.

So, we can ignore these R packages when we're looking for dependencies to bundle with a webR+shinylive app. In webR 0.4.1, these packages will also be ignored when invoking `webr::install()`, and I'm told the native `install.packages()` already does the same.

See https://github.com/quarto-ext/shinylive/issues/59 for discussion.

c.f. https://github.com/r-wasm/webr/pull/463

title: Restore short R version in r-wasm repo URLs
description:
For a previous version of webR, we required the full R version to be included as part of r-wasm repo URLs for Emscripten ABI compatability reasons. This was a temporary measure and is no longer required for the latest release of webR.

This PR restores the original short R versioning in repo.r-wasm.org URLs, matching the base R and r-universe behaviour.

The TODO mentioned combining two functions (one for r-wasm, the other for r-universe) but I've decided not to in case we diverge again in the future. Instead, I've just abstracted out the logic for showing a warning message when native and Wasm package versions don't match.

title: feat: Customize export template and parameters
description:
Fixes #32
Pairs with https://github.com/posit-dev/shinylive/pull/144

Adds `template_dir` and `template_params` to `shinylive::export()`.

* `template_dir` allows users to customize the `index.html` file used by the exported app. This argument takes a path that, effectively, supercedes the path in the shinylive assets.
* `template_params` takes a list of template parameters. https://github.com/posit-dev/shinylive/pull/144/files introduces a new set of template params, e.g. `{{ title }}`. This argument also covers parameters introduced by custom templates, or future parameters added to the default shinylive template.

I initially used `glue::glue()` for the interpolation, but realized while working on the Python side of this change that that it won't be easy to replicate glue's interpolation behavior in Python.

Instead, I decided to use `whisker` so that both implementations can use [mustache](https://mustache.github.io/) for templating. I think this is a net win, as it allows for more powerful templating for power users without overly complicating the feature.

title: feat: Choose asset version at export
description:
Adds a new `assets_version` argument to `export()` that then propagates throughout the export process. This makes it possible to use `shinylive::export()` with asset versions other than the one currently used by default in the package.

The primary use case was to allow me to use the 0.4.1 assets even though the package is currently tied to 0.3.0. I used this to be able to use the preview version of shinylive with the wasm package library before it was officially tied to the package.

With this change `assets_version()` reports the current default version used by the package. Users may either set `assets_version` when calling `export()` or they may use the `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION` envvar to achieve the same thing. The envvar is necessary for CI environments where it's easy to set this variable but hard to provide a version to the right function call, which is hidden from the user inside a GitHub workflow.

Note that setting `assets_version` is enough, `assets_ensure()` will find the require assets version and download it as necessary.

We don't currently do minimum version checking; in the future we would still update the default assets version used by the package. If we ever have a breaking change where the `r-shinylive` package would be incompatible with older versions, we could include a version check in a central place, probably in `assets_ensure()`.

title: feat: envvar to allow downloading core packges in wasm package library
description:
Adds an envvar `SHINYLIVE_DOWNLOAD_WASM_CORE_PACKAGES` geared toward advanced users who want to use the development versions of packages that are included in the core set of packages used with shinylive.

The goal is that `SHINYLIVE_DOWNLOAD_WASM_CORE_PACKAGES` could take a list of packages that would normally **not** be download with the wasm package bundle because they appear in the core package list and mark them as "downloadable".

In particular, I needed this to be able to include the in-development version of bslib in workshop materials.

Some packages are patched in the `r-wasm` org and probably shouldn't be downloadable, but I'm also assuming that someone using this envvar will have that context. (In other words, this is an advanced usage feature.)

title: Switch from base64enc to jsonlite
description:
Base64 decoding of files in `app.json` is currently broken by the changes in #72. This PR switches to `jsonlite`'s implementation (removing a dependency), and fixes the problem.

Also, use `try()` in the case of binary files so as to recover from a base64 decode error, since binary files likely don't affect the result of renv package dependency resolution in any case.

description:

A first-pass implementation of #63.

Exports shinylive apps with Wasm R binary packages downloaded and included in `.../shinylive/webr/packages`. Metadata is stored in `.../shinylive/webr/packages/metadata.rds` and loaded at runtime.

For `shinylive::export()`, you can disable Wasm package bundling with `wasm_packages = FALSE`. And disable using the cache with `package_cache = FALSE`. Both are `TRUE` by default, meaning Wasm packages will be downloaded and bundled.

For Quarto documents with embedded R Shinylive apps, `quarto_ext.R` is updated so that `app.json` bundles passed to the `shinylive` R package are decoded onto disk, and then R Wasm binaries are downloaded using the same tools as created for `shinylive::export()`. Finally the resulting list of binaries are passed back to Quarto as HTML dependencies.

Metadata is merged over subsequent runs since (in e.g. Quarto docs) we can have multiple `app.json` bundles, and we want _all_ referenced packages to be available in the static assets.

---

Recursive dependencies are resolved using the `pkgdepends` package. This can get slow for large local package libraries (My R library has all of CRAN installed, for unrelated reasons, and so it takes a few seconds to resolve). We might want to think about how we could make use of `r-lib/pkgcache` in future. This should be "fine" for the moment, though.

---

Note: Requires the `shinylive` assets bundle from https://github.com/posit-dev/shinylive/pull/121

title: feat(gha): Add `app-dir` input to the deploy-app reusable workflow
description:
## Problem

The reusable `deploy-app.yaml` workflow always treats the repo root as the app. It runs `renv::dependencies(".")` and `shinylive::export(".", "site")`. Apps kept in a subfolder, such as `app/`, can't use it.

Keeping the app in a subfolder is also the safest layout when an exported site is committed to the repo, for example in `docs/` for GitHub Pages. With the app in the root, a stale export inside the app folder can be bundled into `app.json`.

## Change

- New optional input `app-dir`, the folder that contains `app.R`, relative to the repo root. The default is `"."`, so existing callers don't change.
- The input goes through an `APP_DIR` environment variable instead of being pasted into the R code.
- The example workflow and the README show how to set `app-dir`.

```yaml
jobs:
  shinylive:
    uses: posit-dev/r-shinylive/.github/workflows/deploy-app.yaml@actions-v1
    with:
      app-dir: app
```

The `actions-v1` tag will need to move to the merge commit before callers can use the new input.

title: fix: Do not download the CRAN `webr` package for webR's built-in `webr` calls
description:
## Problem

webR ships its own R package named `webr`, which provides `webr::install()`, `webr::mount()` and similar functions. CRAN also has an unrelated package named `webr`, and the webR package repository builds it.

When an app calls `webr::install("markdown")`, `renv::dependencies()` reports `webr`. `export()` then downloads the CRAN `webr` package and its dependencies (moonBook, rrtable, ztable, flextable, psych, vcd, ...). For one real app, that was 126 extra packages (about 127 MB). shinylive mounts every package in `metadata.rds` at startup, so all of them were downloaded before the app could run.

## Change

`webr` is always added to the list of packages that are never downloaded. This covers both direct `webr::` calls and `webr` showing up as a resolved dependency. It still applies if `webr` is listed in `SHINYLIVE_DOWNLOAD_WASM_CORE_PACKAGES`, because webR loads its own `webr` package before the app runs, so the CRAN package could never be loaded in Shinylive anyway.

The `wasm_packages` docs in `?export` and NEWS explain this. Apps that need functions from the CRAN `webr` package should copy them into the app's code.

## Effect on the real app

On the app that showed this problem, the bundled packages dropped from 134 (about 127 MB) to the 10 the app actually needs (about 5.7 MB).

title: feat!: Float the Shinylive assets version within a series
description:
## Summary

The R package no longer pins one Shinylive assets version. New assets patch releases reach users without a CRAN release, which removes the need to resubmit to CRAN for each shiny / webR update.

* **Default is a series.** `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION_DEFAULT <- "0.10.*"` replaces the pinned `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION` constant. `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION_FALLBACK <- "0.10.16"` is the known-good version used when no match is known. A new minor series (0.11) is only used by default after a package release, since it may move the files the package reads.
* **Inputs.** `export(assets_version=)`, `assets_download(version=)`, `assets_ensure(version=)`, and the `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION` env var accept an exact version (`"0.10.16"`), a series (`"0.11.*"`), or `"latest"`. Their version arguments default to `NULL` (as `export()` already did). A non-`NULL` argument beats the env var, which beats the default series (empty env var = unset).
* **`versions.json` + daily check** (new `R/assets_version.R`). Stored in the assets cache dir with `checked_at`, `latest`, `versions`, and `error` after a failed check. Checked at most once a day, once an hour after a failure, and always for `"latest"`. The check is a HEAD request to `releases/latest` (redirect, no API rate limit, 1s connect timeout). The full release list is fetched with `gh` only when the latest tag changed. Failures keep the old list. Written atomically; read-only caches are tolerated. Never runs during CRAN checks.
* **Resolution.** Highest match from the release list and the downloaded folders, remembered for the R session so one export checks at most once. Building a bundle URL never downloads. `"latest"` warns when its check fails. Offline: falls back to the highest downloaded match with a warning, then to the fallback version, then a clear error.
* **Quarto.** Only `extension info` checks GitHub, and it no longer downloads. The later commands (`base-htmldeps`, `language-resources`, `app-resources`) run in their own R processes and only read the `versions.json` that `info` just saved, so one render uses one version.
* **Other changes.** Downloads extract to a temp folder and move into place (and keep a folder another R process just made). A re-download moves the old folder aside before replacing it. `assets_cleanup()` keeps the newest version of each series plus a pinned version, and removes temp files older than 10 minutes left by interrupted downloads. `assets_info()` shows the default series and last check and never downloads. The `update-assets-version` skill now only covers a new series or a fallback bump; patch releases need nothing.

**Behavior change:** `assets_version()` is no longer constant. It can change over time and may use the network or download assets. Existing code keeps working, so NEWS files this under New features rather than Breaking changes.

Known gaps:
* A backport release not marked "latest" is not seen until the latest tag changes again.
* Documents with both R and Python blocks fail in Quarto when py-shinylive's pinned version differs from the version R picks. Tracked in posit-dev/py-shinylive#69.

## Verification

```r
pak::pak("posit-dev/r-shinylive@schloerke/shinylive-assets-versioning")
shinylive::assets_info()        # default series, resolved version, last check
shinylive::assets_version()     # newest 0.10.x, e.g. "0.10.16"
# versions.json in the cache dir now lists the releases

Sys.setenv(SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION = "latest")
shinylive:::assets_version_reset(); shinylive::assets_version()

app <- system.file("examples", "01_hello", package = "shiny")
shinylive::export(app, tempfile(), assets_version = "0.10.15")  # pin exactly
```

To check offline behavior, turn off the network and rerun `export()`: it uses the downloaded assets.

title: fix: Address bugs and doc errors found by the memory bank
description: Fixes the "Behavior", "Docs", and "Tests and CI" items in [posit-dev/r-shinylive#216](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/216). Each item is its own commit, and each code fix adds a test that failed before the fix. Code fixes: - **Assets:** `assets_dir()` and `assets_ensure()` use `dir`. `assets_info()` works with no assets installed. Stray `shinylive-*` entries in the cache are skipped. `assets_ensure()` shows the folder it creates. `check_assets_url()` returns `FALSE` on a 404. - **Quarto dependencies:** `shinylive_common_dep_htmldep()` uses `version` and runs `match.arg()` on `dep_type`. - **Wasm packages:** - `max_filesize` is parsed by a new `parse_max_filesize()`. `"Inf"`, `"NA"`, and `"-1"` turn the limit off. Bad values like `""` warn and use the default instead of quietly turning the limit off. A value that is not a single number or string is an error. - The size limit is checked on every export, not just on download. A package dropped for its size stays cached with its size saved: it is downloaded again only once the limit allows that size, and the warning shows on each export until then. A cached package over a new, smaller limit is dropped too (or is an error when the limit is set). The warning or error comes before any file is deleted, so an error leaves the files and `metadata.rds` as they were. - **Export:** - Keep the app and the export in separate folders, like `export("myapp", "site")`. `destdir` equal to `appdir` (`export(".", ".")`) or holding it (`export("myapp", ".")`) is now an error instead of an empty `app.json`. A `destdir` inside `appdir` (`export(".", "site")`) still works but is not recommended. The `destdir` docs and the README say so. - Non-UTF-8 text files are stored as binary. - An app folder named `venv`/`rsconnect`, and mixed relative/absolute paths, are handled. Paths are compared with a new `comparable_path()`: absolute, with symlinks resolved (also in the parent of a path that does not exist yet, through `full_path()`), and lower case on Windows and macOS. It is only used to compare paths, never to name files. - A new `check_subdir()` rejects `..` and treats `.` as no subdir. - Template files are overwritten on re-export. - `unlink_path()` removes files, so `create_copy_fn(overwrite = TRUE)` works. - The "copies differ" message respects `quiet`. - **Quarto `app-resources`:** paths are checked by their parts, with `fs::is_absolute_path()` catching drive letters and `~` paths. Binary files that can't be decoded are an error. Docs, tests, and CI: - Roxygen, README, NEWS, `examples/README.md`, and `DESCRIPTION` errors are fixed. - `TEST_ASSETS=1` now enables the asset tests. - The Quarto tests no longer delete the session temp folder. - The spelling test now fails on errors. `JSON`, `pak`, `repo`, `repo's`, `stdin`, `stdout`, `subfolder`, and `subdir` are added to the WORDLIST, since older spelling dictionaries flag some of them. - A no-op `sub()` is dropped from the integration job. - Duplicate and unescaped ignore patterns are removed. NEWS bullets are added, and the memory-bank docs now match the new behavior. Not changed: the "Possibly by design" items in the issue (old packages kept in `metadata.rds`, no on-disk check on a cache hit, `writeLines()` trailing newline, empty `SHINYLIVE_WASM_PACKAGES`/`SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION`, empty files as `[]`, `assets_info(quiet = TRUE)` visibility). The `assets_info()` docs now describe its visibility. The "On push events" comment in `deploy-app.yaml` is left alone, so that the `actions-v1` tag does not need to move. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

title: fix: Use the webR R version from the exported assets when bundling WebAssembly packages
description:
Closes #209

## Summary

`export()` and the Quarto extension picked WebAssembly package binaries with the hard-coded `WEBR_R_VERSION`, no matter which assets were used. With a different `assets_version`, this could bundle binaries that the assets' webR can't load. This already happens today: assets 0.8.0 through 0.10.0 ship webR on R 4.4.1, but binaries were taken from `contrib/4.6`.

- New `assets_webr_r_version(version)` in `R/assets.R`. It ensures the assets are present and reads `Version:` from `shinylive/webr/vfs/usr/lib/R/library/translations/DESCRIPTION`. This file exists in assets 0.8.0, 0.9.0, 0.10.0 and 0.10.16. If it is missing, it errors and says to delete the assets folder so it is downloaded again.
- `WEBR_R_VERSION` is removed. Wasm packages already needed assets 0.8.0 or later, so there is no release that needs a fallback. `wasm_packages_able()` now checks `< 0.8.0` so the rule matches its message.
- The R version is passed from `export()` and the Quarto extension through `download_wasm_packages()` and `prepare_wasm_metadata()` to `get_wasm_assets()`. The new `wasm_contrib_url(repo, r_version)` builds the repo URL.
- Package cache: binary file names (`scales_1.4.0.tgz`) are the same across R versions, so a cached binary for the old R version would be kept. Each `metadata.rds` entry now stores `_webr_r_version`. Entries for another R version, or without it (from older shinylive), are dropped and their folders deleted, so they are downloaded again. The full R version is compared, so a patch bump (4.6.0 -> 4.6.1) also re-downloads. Existing caches will re-download once.
- A test checks the R version of the default assets, and the update-assets-version skill says to update it when the webR R version changes.

The shinylive browser code only reads `name`, `path`, `cached`, `assets` and `type` from `metadata.rds` entries, so the new `_webr_r_version` field doesn't affect it.

## Verification

```r
# Older assets ship webR on R 4.4.1
shinylive:::assets_webr_r_version("0.9.0")
#> [1] "4.4.1"

# Binaries now come from contrib/4.4 for these assets
shinylive::export("myapp", "site", assets_version = "0.9.0")
```

title: test: Compare assets versions as versions in the export template test
description:
The "export with template" test skipped itself with `skip_if(assets_version() <= "0.4.1")`. That compares two strings as text, so `"0.10.16" <= "0.4.1"` is `TRUE` and the test never ran.

Compare against `package_version("0.4.1")` so the check uses version order and the test runs again.

title: feat(gha): Add shinylive-version and assets-version inputs to the deploy-app workflow
description:
The `deploy-app.yaml` reusable workflow always installs shinylive from GitHub `main` and exports with that package's default assets. A caller can't pin either one, so any merge to `main` here can change every site that uses `@actions-v1`.

## Changes

**New inputs in `deploy-app.yaml`:**
- `shinylive-version`: the {pak} reference to install, such as `shinylive` (CRAN), `shinylive@0.5.0` or `posit-dev/r-shinylive` (GitHub). The default stays `posit-dev/r-shinylive` until the next CRAN release (see the release bullet below).
- `assets-version`: the assets version passed to `export()`.
  - `""` (the default) uses the installed package's assets version, so the assets always match the package.
  - A version such as `0.10.16` (or `v0.10.16`) pins it.
  - `latest` looks up the newest [posit-dev/shinylive release](https://github.com/posit-dev/shinylive/releases) at run time.

  The docs say that assets other than the package's default may not work with that package. Each package version is built for the webR R version of its own assets, and it uses that R version to pick the WebAssembly package binaries it bundles.

**Bug fixes in `deploy-app.yaml`:**
- `cache-version` read `github.event.inputs.cache-version`, which only holds manual-run inputs. A caller's value was ignored. It now reads `inputs.cache-version`. Callers rebuild their package cache once.
- Upload and deploy only ran on `refs/heads/main`. They now run on the caller's default branch, so repos using `master` also deploy. Scheduled runs also deploy, since they always run on the default branch.

**Test.** `.github/workflows/test-deploy-app.yaml` calls this PR's copy of `deploy-app.yaml` and exports `.github/deploy-app-test/app.R` in two setups:
- this PR's package (`posit-dev/r-shinylive#<PR>`) with its default assets
- the CRAN package with `assets-version: latest`

It runs on pull requests that change the workflow, the test, the test app or the package. It never runs on `main`, because there the workflow would deploy to this repo's GitHub Pages and replace the pkgdown site.

**Agent skills** (in `.agents/skills/`, linked from `.claude/skills`):
- `update-assets-version`: the steps of an assets update (`R/version.R`, the `NEWS.md` bullet, the examples that name a version). An assets update needs no workflow change or `actions-v1` move.
- `update-actions-tag`: when to move `actions-v1` (after a merged change to the workflow or `examples/`, and after the CRAN switch), when not to, and how to do it safely.

`examples/README.md` now points to `update-actions-tag` instead of listing the steps. Its old steps had two errors: `git push --tags` is rejected for a moved tag, and they said changes to `examples/` need no tag move, but `usethis::use_github_action()` copies the example from the tag.

**Release bullet.** `R/release.R` adds `release_bullets()`, so `usethis::use_release_issue()` adds this item to the release checklist:

> After CRAN accepts the release, change the `shinylive-version` input default in `.github/workflows/deploy-app.yaml` from `posit-dev/r-shinylive` to `shinylive`, so the workflow installs the CRAN release. Then move the `actions-v1` tag to that commit (see `.agents/skills/update-actions-tag/SKILL.md`). Remove this bullet afterwards.

**Docs.** The README and `examples/deploy-app.yaml` show the new inputs.

## After merging

Move `actions-v1` to the merge commit so callers get the new inputs (see the `update-actions-tag` skill). Existing callers see no change: they still install from GitHub `main` and use that package's assets.

Callers can't set `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION` as an environment variable instead. GitHub does not pass a caller's workflow-level `env` to a reusable workflow, and a job that calls one can't set `env`. The input is the only way to choose the assets.

title: fix: Match py-shinylive follow-ups for assets version resolution
description:
Closes [posit-dev/r-shinylive#225](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/225).

These changes make R behave like py-shinylive, which made the same fixes in [posit-dev/py-shinylive#71](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/71) and [posit-dev/py-shinylive#76](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/76). No py-shinylive change is needed.

## Changes

* **A custom `url` never uses GitHub.** With `url` set (such as a mirror), `assets_ensure()` and `assets_download()` choose the version from `versions.json` and the downloaded folders only (`check = FALSE, download = FALSE`), then download from `url`. For a series or `"latest"`, if the tarball holds a different matching version, that folder is used. For an exact version, a tarball without `shinylive-<version>` is a clear error. The download steps moved into an internal `download_assets_tarball()`.
* **Stalled downloads time out.** `req_options(low_speed_limit = 1, low_speed_time = 60)`: no data for 60 seconds fails, but a slow download that keeps getting data finishes.
* **A bad `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION` names the env var.** `assets_version_input()` checks it ("Bad `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION` environment variable."), and `assets_cleanup_keep_default()` uses it.
* **Keep the fallback error.** The final "Can't download" error adds "The fallback v0.10.16 also failed: <reason>".
* **Say when GitHub is checked again.** The failed-check warning names when the check failed and when it runs again (`checked_at + VERSIONS_RETRY_HOURS`). A comment says why it repeats in every R process.
* **Stricter latest tag pattern:** `v[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)*$`.
* **Test the "releases only move forward" assumption**, so a change to it is on purpose.

NEWS and `memory-bank/assets.md` are updated.

title: fix: Only save versions.json once the chosen assets are downloaded
description:
Closes [posit-dev/r-shinylive#223](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/223). Matches the change in [posit-dev/py-shinylive#72](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/pull/72).

## Problem

`versions.json` was saved right after the GitHub check, before the chosen version was downloaded. If the download then failed, an older local version was used, but `versions.json` still named the newer release. Quarto's later commands (`check = FALSE`) only read that file, so they picked the newer release and tried to download it. If that worked, one render mixed two assets versions. The same happens across packages, since R and Python share `versions.json`.

## Rule

`versions.json` only names a version once it is downloaded.

- `check_versions_info()` (was `update_versions_info()`) runs the check and returns the new info. It writes nothing.
- `resolve_assets_version()` saves the new info only when a check ran and the chosen version is in the local cache (already there or just downloaded). `check = FALSE` never writes. A read-only cache is still ignored.
- If the chosen version fails to download and an older local version is used, the saved info leaves out the newer releases in that series (other series are kept), sets `latest` to `null` so the next check fetches the full list, and records the download error so the next check runs within the hour.
- The "may not be the newest" warning now says "The last check for new Shinylive assets releases failed", as in py-shinylive.

## Behavior change

The Quarto `extension info` command now downloads the assets it reports, as py-shinylive already does. Without the download, the new version would not be saved, and `info` would report a different version than the later commands use.

## py-shinylive

No follow-up needed: py-shinylive already has this rule.

title: ci: Resolve the assets cache key without downloading the assets
description:
Since [posit-dev/r-shinylive#218](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/218), `shinylive::assets_version()` downloads the version it picks. The `R-CMD-check-test-assets` job called it to build the cache key, before `actions/cache` restores the cache, so every run downloaded the assets and the cache saved no time.

The step now calls `shinylive:::resolve_assets_version(..., download = FALSE)`. It still checks GitHub for the newest release in the series, but it only writes `versions.json`. The key still changes when a new patch release comes out, so tests run against the new assets.

Also replaces the pitfall added in [posit-dev/r-shinylive#220](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/220) with a note on why the step must not download.

title: docs(agents): Update the memory bank for floating assets versions
description:
[posit-dev/r-shinylive#218](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/218) changed code that three memory-bank docs still described the old way.

- `testing.md`: add `test-assets_version.R` to the file table, list the newer `test-assets.R` tests, and include both in the offline tests note.
- `ciAndTooling.md`: `release_bullets()` now adds two items; the `assets-version` input of `deploy-app.yaml` now gets the newest release in the series when empty and passes series through; new pitfall: the test-assets job's cache key step calls `assets_version()`, which now downloads the assets before `actions/cache` restores them, so the cache saves no download time.
- `export.md`: fix the pitfall about `export()` order. The assets version is now resolved after the argument checks.

title: docs(agents): Add steps to keep py-shinylive in sync
description:
## Summary

Adds a "Keep py-shinylive in sync" section to `AGENTS.md`. It lists what the R and Python packages share (the Quarto extension commands and JSON, the assets cache folder and `versions.json`, and how the assets version is chosen). It asks contributors to check whether each feature or bug fix also needs a py-shinylive change, and to open a linked issue or PR there.

[posit-dev/r-shinylive#218](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/218) is an example: it needed a matching change in py-shinylive ([posit-dev/py-shinylive#69](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/69)) so Quarto documents with both R and Python blocks keep rendering.

py-shinylive gets the matching section in its own `AGENTS.md`.
